items.label: 1C
items.claim: UKHSA's successor Illumina consumables ceiling implies only about 33% more spend per year than the prior contract, which is well below 25-30% annual Gb growth compounded over the gap.
items.detail: The prior UKHSA direct award (National Microbiology Framework Lot 2) ran 17 Jan 2022 to 16 Jan 2025 with a total value of £9.8M, or about £3.27M/yr over 3.0 years. The successor call-off (28 Nov 2025 to 30 Aug 2028) is £12.0M over about 2.75 years, or about £4.36M/yr, which is +33%. The midpoints are about 3.5 years apart (mid-2023 to early 2027), so the ceiling grows about 8.6%/yr ((1.333)^(1/3.5) -1). That is far below Illumina's 25-30% Gb growth, which implies flat-ish volume, lower unit prices, or a conservative ceiling. Caveats: ceilings are not spend, the contract is a public-health lab covering all Illumina platforms (not NovaSeq X specifically), and the Jan-Nov 2025 gap period is unknown.
items.quote: awarded a contract to Illumina Cambridge Limited for the provision of its proprietary consumables
items.why_new: F019 gave only the £12M figure; this adds the £9.8M predecessor and the per-year growth arithmetic.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: A UK NHS-area buyer in Leeds signed a NovaSeq 6000 maintenance call-off for calendar 2026, so 6000s are still being kept in service there.
items.detail: A Contracts Finder notice published 11 Feb 2026 records a £119,360.40 call-off from a framework for maintaining a NovaSeq 6000, running 18 Jan 2026 to 17 Jan 2027, awarded to Illumina Cambridge Ltd. This is a 12-month renewal of service on a 6000, not a retirement. It is a single-site data point, and the notice does not say how many 6000s are covered or their consumables use.
items.why_new: This is a dated public-sector 6000 service renewal in 2026; the known 6000 evidence is mostly company statements and core price sheets.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Public buyers are still buying NovaSeq X Plus systems and are replacing sequencers, which points to conversion continuing in UK public labs.
items.detail: A March 2024 award for a NovaSeq X Plus system totalled £1,115,627, with a term to 19 Mar 2025, and the buyer is at a Leeds address. UKHSA awarded £323,929.84 (20 Feb to 31 Mar 2026) to replace sequencing equipment across its Genomics laboratory networks. APHA awarded £354,823.10 for high-throughput NGS sequencers (Dec 2025, to 31 Dec 2026). These support the idea that UK labs refresh onto new hardware, not that they stay on old 6000s.
items.why_new: Dated UK public-sector hardware refresh awards with values; none are in the known list.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: UK public buyers award Illumina consumables by direct award on a sole-supplier basis, so there is no tender competition on price.
items.detail: The 2021 AFBI MiSeq award (£230K ex-VAT, 5 years, concluded 5 Jul 2021) was a direct award because Illumina is the sole supplier of servicing and reagents for its machines. NHS Grampian's £198,846 genetics reagents award (Feb 2026) cites only 'Direct Award to existing supplier'. UKHSA's £9.8M and £12M contracts are also direct awards or call-offs. This shows lock-in for existing platforms, which cuts against pricing pressure on installed machines. The tender mechanics also mean discounts are negotiated privately, which is consistent with large accounts getting bigger extra discounts, but no discount figure is published.
items.source_name: BidsFactory (UK FTS 018331-2026) and Find a Tender 015684-2021
items.why_new: Gives the stated justification text for the UK direct awards; the known list has none of it.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: The UKHSA 'framework' structure contains a competitive layer for Illumina platforms, but the latest notice shows no price concession disclosed.
items.detail: APHA's Aug 2024 call-off 'Sequencing Reagents and Consumables (Illumina, UKHSA Framework Call-off)' was £1,598,054, so smaller UK agencies buy Illumina consumables off the UKHSA framework. That pooled buying gives volume leverage to a central buyer. The notices show no discount schedule, so the evidence cannot show whether the pricing falls over time.
items.why_new: Adds an extra £1.6M call-off from the UKHSA framework not in the known list.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Combined UK public-sector Illumina awards on the bidsfactory company page are small and do not show strong volume acceleration.
items.detail: BidsFactory shows 20 awards (12 service, 8 supply) to Illumina Cambridge. The itemised ones are UKHSA £12.0M (Nov 2025), AFBI £2.7M (Jul 2026, benchtop sequencer plus consumables and servicing over ten years) and a UKRI sequencer relocation at £11K (Sep 2026). The 10-year AFBI deal is about £0.27M/yr, which is a tiny run rate, and the page's own totals conflict (£3.1M vs $17.5M). Treat this as a size check on UK public demand, not a trend.
items.why_new: AFBI £2.7M ten-year award and the company-page tally are not in the known list.

notes: Official Contracts Finder and Find a Tender pages returned 403, so the direct-award justification text, discount schedules and volume bands for 031102-2025 could not be read. The notices appear to contain no unit prices, so the source is of limited value. Remaining ideas: the 13 Apr 2023 UKHSA modification notice (803965cc...) and the 2022 UKHSA notice (ac02129a...), if they can be opened by another method, to see whether the £9.8M was changed during its term.
